purpose: Matt's hand ratings of real site lines and of non-product situations written three ways. The real lines calibrate the voice judge; the situations describe the style he is going for. Ratings are recorded in ratings-2026-11-06.md once given.

scale.us: Sounds like us: an experienced recruiter would say it to a candidate, and it says the thing.
scale.flat: Fine, but any product could say it.
scale.no: Wrong: a coined word, a hedge, a slogan, a joke in a serious moment, or it makes the reader translate.

situations.situation: A café's sign when the wifi is down
situations.A: Wifi’s down. We’ve called; no fix time yet. Coffee works.
situations.B: The wifi is out today. Sorry for the inconvenience.
situations.C: Our wifi has taken the day off! Great excuse to actually talk to someone.

situations.situation: Texting a friend whose interview went badly
situations.A: That sucks. Want to walk through what they asked? Half of these are the interviewer, not you.
situations.B: You’ve got this!! Their loss. The right one is coming.
situations.C: Sorry to hear that. Let me know if you want to talk.

situations.A: Dr. Ruiz is out Thursday. Your 2:10 moves to Monday the 14th at 2:10 unless you tell us otherwise.
situations.B: Due to unforeseen circumstances, your appointment has been rescheduled. We apologize for any inconvenience.
situations.C: Heads up: Thursday’s appointment needs to move. Reply with a day that works and we’ll sort it.

situations.situation: A friend's note on your cover letter
situations.A: The second paragraph is the real letter. Cut the first one and start there.
situations.B: Great start! Maybe consider tightening the intro a little? Overall really strong.
situations.C: Your opening reads like a job description. Tell them the thing only you can say.

situations.situation: A hardware store's return policy sign
situations.A: Returns within 30 days with the receipt. Opened paint is yours.
situations.B: We gladly accept returns within 30 days of purchase with a valid receipt. Some exclusions apply.
situations.C: Changed your mind? No problem. Bring it back within 30 days with your receipt.

situations.A: Flight 212 to Denver is delayed about 40 minutes for a late inbound crew. New boarding time is 6:50.
situations.B: We apologize for the delay. Flight 212 will now board at 6:50. Thank you for your patience.
situations.C: Denver folks: the crew is landing now. Boarding at 6:50. Grab a snack.

situations.situation: A gym closing early to clean
situations.A: Closing at 8 tonight to deep-clean the floors. Open at 5 a.m. as usual.
situations.B: We’ll be closing early tonight at 8pm for maintenance. Thank you for understanding!
situations.C: Floors get a scrub tonight. Out by 8, back at 5.

situations.situation: A running coach after a slow race
situations.A: You went out 20 seconds too fast and paid for it at mile 10. Pacing, not fitness. Fixable.
situations.B: Tough day, but every race teaches you something. Proud of you for finishing.
situations.C: The result’s the result. We’ll look at the splits Tuesday.

situations.situation: A museum label beside a painting
situations.A: Painted the year her studio flooded. The water line is still visible in the lower left.
situations.B: This evocative work explores themes of loss, memory and resilience.
situations.C: Oil on canvas, 1912. Gift of the artist’s estate.

situations.A: Sorry for the slow reply. Answer below.
situations.B: Apologies for the delayed response; it’s been a hectic week on my end!
situations.C: Late, and no good reason. Here’s the answer.

situations.situation: A landlord's note about the elevator
situations.A: The elevator is out until Tuesday; the part is on order. The stairs are lit and open. Ring 1B if you need a hand with groceries.
situations.B: Please be advised the elevator is temporarily out of service. We appreciate your patience.
situations.C: Elevator’s down till Tuesday. Think of it as leg day.

situations.situation: A tax service's confirmation page after filing
situations.A: Filed. The IRS usually confirms within 48 hours; we’ll email you when they do.
situations.B: Congratulations, your return has been successfully submitted!
situations.C: Done. Go do something more fun.
